_meta.description: Scenario -> legal statement, condition, forum, citation. The recourse router reads the law from here; AI only classifies the scenario and phrases the output. No legal conclusion is AI-generated. Not legal advice. This is a demonstration pack (lighter than the Kenya pack) proving the model ports to South Africa by swapping data.
_meta.disclaimer: This information is not legal advice. Recourse depends on the specific facts. Statements are conditional.

scenarios.title: A lender is harassing you or misusing your personal information
scenarios.law_statement: The Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA) governs how your personal information may be processed. Misusing your data or contacts to harass or shame you can breach POPIA, which the Information Regulator enforces.
scenarios.condition: Applies where a lender processed your personal information without a lawful basis, or used it for abusive collection.
scenarios.citation_date: POPIA, Act 4 of 2013; Information Regulator complaints (Form 5)

scenarios.title: They are taking / threatening to take your financed asset
scenarios.law_statement: Under the National Credit Act 34 of 2005, a credit provider must follow lawful enforcement, including a section 129 default notice, before enforcing or repossessing. Repossession without following the Act's process can be challenged.
scenarios.condition: Your repossession MAY be unlawful IF no proper section 129 notice was served or the process was not followed. This depends on your agreement and the facts; verify before acting.

scenarios.title: The lender misled you, hid the cost, or lent recklessly
scenarios.law_statement: The National Credit Act 34 of 2005 requires clear cost-of-credit disclosure and prohibits reckless credit granting (lending without proper affordability assessment). Reckless credit can be set aside or the debt re-arranged by a court or the National Consumer Tribunal.
scenarios.condition: Applies where cost/terms were not properly disclosed, or credit was granted without a proper affordability assessment.

scenarios.title: An unregistered lender is chasing you for repayment
scenarios.law_statement: Credit providers must be registered with the National Credit Regulator (NCR) under the National Credit Act. An unregistered provider operates unlawfully, and the enforceability of such credit is challengeable.
scenarios.condition: Applies IF the lender is not registered with the NCR. Confirm registration status first.

scenarios.title: You were wrongly listed by a credit bureau
scenarios.law_statement: Credit bureaus are regulated under the National Credit Act and POPIA. You have the right to dispute inaccurate credit information; the bureau must investigate, and unresolved disputes can be taken to the National Credit Regulator.
scenarios.condition: Applies where a listing is inaccurate, based on a disputed debt, or made without a proper basis.
scenarios.citation_date: National Credit Act; NCR credit-information dispute guidelines

scenarios.title: You want to recover money (a refund, an overpayment, or a small debt)
scenarios.law_statement: The Small Claims Court hears civil money claims up to a set limit (R20,000 at the time of writing) with no lawyer required; you represent yourself. It is a direct, low-cost route to recover money owed to you.
scenarios.condition: Applies where your claim is for money within the Small Claims Court limit. Confirm the current monetary limit and procedure with the court before filing.
scenarios.citation_date: Small Claims Courts Act 61 of 1984 (limit set by the Minister; verify current amount)
